dish: Okinawan tempura — fish, squid (ika) and mozuku tempura fried to order
n: Ōshiro Tempura, Ōjima (大城てんぷら店)
w: One of the three tempura stands on 'tempura island' Ōjima, under shade trees right by the water; fish, vegetable and squid tempura are fried after you order, for a few coins apiece.

dish: Same-day catch sashimi, seafood rice bowls and mozuku at the fishermen's market
n: Ōjima Imaiyu Market, Nanjō (奥武島いまいゆ市場)
address: Entrance of Ōjima island, Tamagusuku Ōjima, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan
w: 'Imaiyu' means 'fresh fish' in Okinawan: a small market at the island entrance selling local catches as sashimi, sushi and seafood bowls, plus produce; an on-site eating space was added so the fish can be eaten looking out over the harbour.

dish: Nūyaru Burger — gōyā (bitter melon) and egg patty burger
address: Yonabaru, Yonabaru-chō, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan
w: Head store of Jef, the Okinawa-only burger chain begun in Yonabaru in 1973 (independent since 1986); its signature Nūyaru Burger tucks an egg-bound gōyā patty into the bun, and the shop hands them to local children on Gōyā Day.

dish: Miyako-grown mango parfait and tropical-fruit soft serve
n: Utopia Farm Miyakojima (ユートピアファーム宮古島)
w: Tropical-fruit farm growing mango, pineapple and dragon fruit, with a parlour serving its own harvest as parfaits, soft serve and roll cake; the whole-Miyako-mango parfait is the order in season.

dish: Frozen apple-mango and mango soft serve
n: Blue Turtle Farm Mango Café, Miyako (ブルータートルファーム マンゴーカフェ)
address: Near Miyako Airport, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan
w: Mango farm café minutes from Miyako Airport serving dense Miyako-mango sweets — frozen whole apple mango and mango soft serve.
